crossing supervisor Listen Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print Content components School crossing supervisors have a much-valued role in Boroondara. On an average school day in Boroondara, they help 9,266 pedestrians to cross the street while 74,426 motor vehicles use our roads during school crossing times. We are always looking for school crossing supervisors. If you are friendly, reliable and flexible, this role is for you. What does a school crossing supervisor do? This paid position gives you the opportunity to get involved in your community and improve road safety for children, people with a disability and the general public who use our 114 school crossings. School crossing supervisors: • work part-time Monday to Friday, from 8 am to 9 am and from 3 pm to 4 pm, during the school term • play an important role in educating children with ‘Stop, Look and Listen’ instructions • are responsible for reporting any road hazards or potential risks • help to encourage active and independent travel. About you We are looking for people aged 18 and older who: • can attend shifts at short notice • have their own reliable transport • are able to work across several locations • can complete the pre-employment medical and police checks. You will have access to a full training program before starting your role. Download the position description School Crossing Supervisor PD 144.04 KB [PDF] 23 November 2022 How to apply Learn more about this rewarding role by reading the position description above. Submit an online application through our Careers website . Attend an interview – meet with one of our Council Officers at Council, located at 8 Inglesby Road in Camberwell. Provide us with relevant employment documents – including your Working With Children Check, Police Check and evidence of your COVID-19 vaccination status. Complete a medical assessment. Apply to become a School Crossings Supervisor We are always recruiting new school crossing supervisors to help people to cross our roads safely at peak school times. Are you passionate about supporting small business? Bring your project support, communication and organisational skills to a role that helps deliver grants, projects and events for Boroondara’s local business community. About the role: Joining our Local Economies Team, you'll support a range of initiatives that strengthen local shopping centres, trader associations and businesses across Boroondara. Reporting to the Coordinator Economic Development, you'll provide project support, stakeholder engagement and administrative coordination across a variety of economic development programs and initiatives. Key responsibilities include: Supporting the planning, delivery and evaluation of economic development projects, programs and events. Providing advice and assistance to businesses, trader associations and community stakeholders. Building and maintaining positive relationships with local traders, businesses and industry partners. Preparing correspondence, reports, presentations and other business documentation. Managing project administration, stakeholder communications and record keeping. Responding to enquiries from businesses, residents and trader associations. Contributing to continuous improvement initiatives and team projects. Undertaking other duties, projects and initiatives as required to support the objectives of the Economic Development team. A current National Police Records Check is required. An Employee Working with Children Check may also be required. More information Refer to the position description or call Maria Cogger, Coordinator Economic Development on 9278 4089 during business hours. How to Apply Apply online by 11:59pm Wednesday 04th November 2026. Applications sent directly to the hiring manager will not be considered. If you want to know more about the benefits of working for the City of Boroondara, please visit our Careers Website. . We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: MCH Nurse (15263) Requisition ID 15263 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Maternal and Child Health Nurse Part time, (0.8FTE) permanent position Continue your professional journey with our highly valued maternal and child health service $ 125,526 - $135,195 (pro rata to be applied) per annum plus Superannuation This is a great opportunity for an enthusiastic Maternal & Child Health Nurse to continue your professional journey with our experienced and cohesive team of MCH Nurses on a permanent part- time basis. A little bit about the role You will work closely with our families to provide advice, support, and guidance through the critical foundational years for each family. The role will be responsible for, but not limited to: Promoting healthy outcomes for children and their families. Providing a comprehensive and focused approach to managing the physical, emotional, or social factors affecting families in contemporary communities. Providing opportunities for social interaction of the parent and child. Providing families with timely, accurate and relevant information and resources to assist them achieve and maintain maximum health potential. Skills and experience to thrive in the role Demonstrated clinical experience in Maternal & Child Health. Commitment to family centred practice within an integrated early years’ service mode. Awareness of child and family health issues, normal child development, family dynamics and promotion of maternal wellbeing. Familiarity with MCH & immunisation programs across Boroondara. Demonstrated awareness of smalltalk, Parent Child Mother Goose and Circle of Security programs. Experience in sleep and settling program delivery, including day stay and outreach services desirable Able to use computer systems, including Microsoft Word, Microsoft Outlook, icope and CDIS. Qualifications & employment requirements Registered General Division 1 Nurse & Midwife with AHPRA registration A post graduate qualification in Maternal & Child Health Nursing IBCLC qualification Immunisation qualification preferred Ability to work independently, and within a multidisciplinary team Commitment to family centred practice within an integrated early years’ service model Demonstrated clinical experience in Maternal & Child Health Aware of child and family health issues, normal child development, family dynamics & promotion of maternal well being High levels of written and oral communication skills Conversant with relevant health promotion issues How to Apply Please submit your application online via the ‘Apply’ button by 11:59pm Thursday 29 October 2026. For any further information please refer to the position description or contact Yvette Carrazzo, Acting Coordinator Maternal and Child Health on 9278 4012 during business hours for a confidential discussion. If you want to know more about the benefits of working for the City of Boroondara, please visit our Careers Website. Applicants must have the right to work in Australia. Council is a child safe organisation and as such, this position requires a satisfactory Working with Children Clearance and National Criminal History check We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state.
